page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a clock speed of up to 4.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Compute capabilities are augmented by hardware instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for deep learning acceleration, alongside 260 MB of shared L3 cache.

Resource allocation is heavily tilted toward memory density, providing 128.0 GB of system RAM, which equates to 32.0 GB per vCPU. The instance also bundles a 945 GB local NVMe SSD for fast temporary scratch space and caching operations. No dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with this instance profile.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core testing reaching the top quartile at 2093.0 and showing strong text processing throughput. However, due to its constrained 4-vCPU footprint, multi-threaded metrics such as stress-ng multi-core and software compilation remain in lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests also register in the lower quartile, recording 34.95 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 24.77 GB/sec for writes.

This server offers high cost efficiency for workloads constrained by per-core software licensing that demand substantial memory footprints. Tradeoffs include low overall parallel compute throughput and limited memory bandwidth relative to larger multithreaded nodes. Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v6 is ideally suited for in-memory caching layers, licensed enterprise relational databases, memory-heavy ETL batch pipelines, and analytics platforms requiring large memory footprints without extensive multi-core compute demands.
